stem:
During a storm, strong wind blows fast over the tin roof of Meena's house in a village near Pune. The roof is lifted upward.
Which explanation is correct?

options.text: The fast-moving air above the roof has lower pressure, so the higher pressure of the still air inside the house pushes the roof upward.
The fast-moving air above the roof has higher pressure, and this higher pressure pushes the roof upward from outside.
The pressure of the fast-moving air above the roof is the same as the pressure inside, so the roof lifts only because of its own weight.
The pressure above the roof is lower simply because it is higher up, whether the air is moving or still.

teacher.key_rationale: Fast-moving air over the roof lowers the pressure above it; the higher pressure of the still air below pushes the roof up. B reverses the pressure–speed relationship, C omits the pressure difference condition, and D attributes the low pressure to position rather than air speed. Key recalculated for the new item.
